summary: A glib hero with two eligible weapons attempts #twoweapon. C can_twoweapon takes its Glib/cursed-secondary arm and drop_uswapwep prints the slip message, clears the secondary slot through do.c:dropz, and drops that weapon. JavaScript refuses at can_twoweapon; the source helper and the worn-slot drop path are both needed.

source.branch: After earlier form, hand, weapon, bimanual, shield, artifact, and corpse tests pass, can_twoweapon sees Glib or a cursed uswapwep. With Glib it skips set_bknown, calls drop_uswapwep, returns FALSE, and dotwoweapon returns ECMD_OK without a time-consuming draw. drop_uswapwep selects one of three messages from cursed and u.twoweap state, then calls do.c:dropx while the object is still uswapwep; do.c:dropz clears that slot before placing the object.
callers: wield.c:dotwoweapon consumes can_twoweapon’s Boolean result before its success-only rnd(20); js/wield.js:dotwoweapon uses the same result.

mkobj.c:curse calls drop_uswapwep when a secondary weapon becomes cursed during active dual wielding; uhitm.c attack processing calls it when the secondary weapon is cursed after an attack. The helper must support these callers as well as can_twoweapon.
dependencies: objnam.c:Yobjnam2 and yobjnam, plus otense and body_part, determine the three complete source messages; implement or wire the consumed naming results rather than hardcoding the selected short sword.

do.c:dropx/freeinv/dropz and worn setters must permit an inventory object currently in uswapwep, clear that slot at dropz’s source position, then place it and update encumbrance. js/do.js:preflight_dropx currently rejects worn or attached objects and its admitted ordinary tail calls dropzAdmitted without slot clearing.
A cursed secondary weapon calls set_bknown before dropping when Glib is false; preserve object-knowledge update and all three message branches.
The selected C step has no RNG; dotwoweapon must return without the success-only rnd(20) draw and preserve earlier wield behavior.

evidence: The saved v13 evaluation at 35deeae3b45298577e919836bfad5c2da681ab6b reports 90/91 screens and cursors, 2291/2291 RNG calls, and first stop at zero-based segment 0 step 90: can_twoweapon’s slippery-or-cursed refusal. The immutable recording is challenges/cases/v13/glib-refuses-dual-wield-and-drops-secondary.session.json, SHA256 cb3edc91389f03c70595f030b6f94c4ef8c4ab688ba28a5001a01621182b8f04.

At C segment 0 step 90, the newline accepting #twoweapon displays “Your short sword slips from your left hand!” with no RNG draw. The independent recipe reaches Glib with an eligible secondary short sword, then attempts the extended command; this verifies the Glib message branch but does not by itself verify the later floor and slot state.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/wield.c:760-831 defines can_twoweapon and drop_uswapwep in order. Lines 797-801 set knowledge conditionally and call drop_uswapwep; lines 808-831 choose one of three messages and call dropx. Upstream do.c:785-842 shows dropx/freeinv and dropz, including setuswapwep(NULL) before floor placement. wield.c:843-864 calls can_twoweapon and skips rnd(20) on false. mkobj.c:1801 and uhitm.c:5843 are other drop_uswapwep call sites.

JavaScript js/wield.js:can_twoweapon around lines 260-270 throws for Glib/cursed secondary and has no drop_uswapwep. Its comment around lines 195-203 still claims Glib cannot arise, contradicted by this C-first v13 case. js/do.js:preflight_dropx around lines 1513-1555 rejects the attached slot and dropx’s admitted path reaches dropzAdmitted without clearing it; align that shared source path while preserving all existing drops.
